It is a shrine that protects {{ill|Ikaho Onsen|ja|伊香保温泉|zh|伊香保溫泉|qid=Q11381013}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine rank}} it was both a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}} and a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. It is regarded as the {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Sannomiya}} of {{ill|Kōzuke Province|Q1054838|qid=Q1054838}}. It is also written as Ikaho Shrine (伊加保神社). It is said that in the past the {{ill|Sannomiya Shrine (Yoshioka Town)|ja|三宮神社 (吉岡町)|qid=Q21655265|lt=Sannomiya Shrine}} (Ōkubo, {{ill|Kitagunma District, Gunma|Q1075450|qid=Q1075450}}, {{ill|Yoshioka, Gunma|Q1154580|qid=Q1154580}}) was the original main shrine. {{nihongo|'''Ikaho Shrine'''|伊香保神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kōzuke Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
The current principal {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100}} are two deities: {{ill|Ōkuninushi|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q276944}} and {{ill|Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto|qid=Q3275687}}, who are worshipped as gods of hot springs and medicine.

However, before the shrine was relocated to the present hot spring area, it is said that a single deity known as “Ikatsubo no Kami,” associated with {{ill|Mountain worship|Q93697439|qid=Q93697439}} of the mountains of “Ikaho” (the former name of this region including Mount Haruna), was enshrined. Another theory, considering the enshrined deity of Sannomiya Shrine, holds that it was {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|Q11404731|qid=Q11404731}}.

== History ==
According to the shrine’s tradition at its current location within the hot spring town, it was founded in {{ill|825|Q24624|qid=Q24624}} ({{ill|Tenchō|de|Tenchō|es|Tenchō|fa|تنچو|fr|Ère Tenchō|ia|Tencho|id|Tenchō|ja|天長|ko|덴초|ru|Тэнтё|simple|Tenchō|sr|Тенчо|th|เท็นโจ|tr|Tenchō|uk|Тентьо|zh|天長 (日本)|zh_yue|天長 (年號)|qid=Q1373138}} 2). The Sannomiya Shrine, regarded as the former main shrine, was founded in {{ill|750|Q23631|qid=Q23631}} ({{ill|Tenpyō-shōhō|Q1373169|qid=Q1373169}} 2).

Its first appearance in the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168}} is in the {{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}} entry for {{ill|835|Q23894|qid=Q23894}} ({{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 2), 9th month, day of Kanmi, where it is listed as a Myōjin shrine. In the 6th year, 6th month, day of Kōshin, it was promoted to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, and thereafter rose in rank, becoming Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade on May 25, {{ill|880|Q23618|qid=Q23618}} ({{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 4), alongside {{ill|Akagi Shrines|Q11635468|qid=Q11635468}}.

In the Engishiki it is recorded as “Ikaho Shrine, Gunma District, Myōjin Taisha,” and was listed as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}. In the “Kōzuke Province Alternating Duty Record Register,” it is ranked Senior First Rank. It is the Sannomiya of Kōzuke Province. However, as its patron clans declined, its influence waned from the medieval period onward.

According to Ozaki Kizao’s “A Study of Ikaho Shrine,” during the early period of mountain worship the shrine was not located at its present site, and Ikaho Shrine existed as a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=satomiya}} at the current site of Sannomiya Shrine. It is also said that the powerful Arima clan (Arima no Kimi) conducted the rites, and that the shrine was originally located in Arima, Shibukawa City, where Wakumikaho Shrine now stands.

By at least the Heian period it was relocated to the Ikaho hot spring town and became the guardian deity of the hot springs. In the early modern period it was called “Onsen Shrine.” Its {{ill|Bettō|Q2900274|qid=Q2900274}} was Onsen-ji Temple, founded during the {{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}}.

As for the shrine buildings, they were completely destroyed by a fire in March {{ill|1878|Q7776|qid=Q7776}} (Meiji 11). The subsidiary Onsen Shrine (formerly the Yakushi Hall of Iō-ji Temple), which had also been lost at the same time, was merged in {{ill|1884|Q7819|qid=Q7819}} (Meiji 17), and the current shrine buildings (temporary shrine) were rebuilt on that site, remaining to the present day.

== Grounds ==
[[File:伊香保神社 Ikaho shrine - panoramio.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Haiden. On the right side of the photo is a pine tree planted by hand by [[Princess Tsunemiya Masako|Princess Masako of Tsunemiya]].]]
The shrine is located at the top of the Ikaho Onsen stone stairway, which is 300 meters long and has 360 steps.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|title=Examples of Tourism Social Capital: The Stone Stairway of Ikaho Onsen|url=https://www.mlit.go.jp/sogoseisaku/region/kankosyakaisihon/83/1002.pdf|publisher=Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism|accessdate=2022-10-23}}</ref>
